DEFINITION · qeva:1:sensitivity@2

Sensitive dependence on initial conditions

A metric dynamical property in which arbitrarily nearby starting states can eventually separate by a fixed positive amount.

editorialdynamics · chaos · analysis

PLAIN

The idea

Sensitivity formalizes one kind of error amplification: no matter how closely two starting states are chosen, some nearby state can eventually move a definite distance away.

EXACT

The compact statement

T has sensitive dependence on initial conditions iff there exists δ>0 such that for every x in X and every ε>0 there exist y in X and n>=0 with d(x,y)<ε and d(T^n(x),T^n(y))>δ.

EXAMPLE

In chaotic systems, small initial discrepancies may become macroscopically separated under iteration.

BOUNDARY / CAVEAT

Sensitivity alone is not a universal definition of chaos.

ASSUMPTIONS

  • (X,d) is a metric space.
  • T:X→X is a map.
